label: Figure 19.5: Minimum wage and structural unemployment
alt: Labour market for farm workers: equilibrium wage $8 at quantity Q. A minimum wage of $11 above equilibrium leaves Q1 workers demanded but Q2 supplied, so the gap from Q1 to Q2 is unemployment.
caption: The free-market wage for farm workers is $8 per hour with Q workers employed. A minimum wage of $11 lies above equilibrium: employers demand only Q<sub>1</sub> workers while Q<sub>2</sub> want to work at that wage, so the gap between Q<sub>1</sub> and Q<sub>2</sub> is unemployment.
